summary: Static/functional validation of /app/deploy/change-domain.sh with a fake docker binary on PATH, plus confirmation of the SSL diagnosis against the live IDCloudHost server. 14/14 harness assertions passed; SSL error reproduced as documented. Caddyfile and docker-compose.yml wiring reviewed and consistent with the switch-domain workflow.

results.docker_invocation: docker compose up -d --build web backend n8n (captured by fake docker)

dns_mismatch_google.input: bash deploy/change-domain.sh google.com (SERVER_IP in .env != google IP)

ssl_diagnosis_live_check.http_80: curl http://IP_SERVER/ -> HTTP 302 redirect to https://crm.IP-SERVER.sslip.io/ (Caddy up and redirecting correctly)
ssl_diagnosis_live_check.https_443: curl https://crm.IP-SERVER.sslip.io/ -> TLSv1.3 alert internal error (0A000438) during handshake, no server certificate presented
ssl_diagnosis_live_check.conclusion: Diagnosis confirmed: Caddy is reachable on 443 but has no cert for crm.IP-SERVER.sslip.io, consistent with Let's Encrypt rate-limit on sslip.io (not on Public Suffix List). Switching to a DuckDNS or own domain via change-domain.sh is the correct remediation.

config_wiring_review.Caddyfile_env_placeholders: Caddyfile uses {$APP_DOMAIN}, {$N8N_DOMAIN}, {$WAHA_DOMAIN}, {$SERVER_IP}, {$ACME_EMAIL} - will pick up new domains on container recreate. OK.
config_wiring_review.docker_compose_web_build_arg: web service passes REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://${APP_DOMAIN} as build arg - therefore --build web in the script is required (frontend is baked at build time). OK.
config_wiring_review.docker_compose_backend_env: backend uses CORS_ORIGINS=https://${APP_DOMAIN}, APP_URL=https://${APP_DOMAIN}, N8N_EMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL, N8N_WAHA_WEBHOOK_URL - all re-read on container recreate. OK.
config_wiring_review.n8n_env: N8N_HOST, WEBHOOK_URL, N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL depend on ${N8N_DOMAIN} - recreated by `up -d n8n`. OK.

critical_code_review_comments: change-domain.sh exit on DNS mismatch happens before backup and sed - good; backup is only created on the happy path (confirmed).

sed regex `^(N8N_[A-Z]+_WEBHOOK_URL=https://)[^/]+` correctly matches both N8N_EMAIL_WEBHOOK_URL and N8N_WAHA_WEBHOOK_URL while leaving N8N_WAHA_WEBHOOK_SECRET untouched (secret has no `_WEBHOOK_URL=` suffix). Verified.

Minor: script does not restart `waha` even though WAHA_DOMAIN changed. Caddyfile picks up the new host, but if WAHA ever reads WAHA_DOMAIN from env in future, it won't be refreshed. Current waha service doesn't use WAHA_DOMAIN env, so this is fine today - just document.
Minor: `grep -E '^SERVER_IP='` + `cut -d= -f2` will mis-handle values containing `=`; fine for an IPv4 but worth noting.
Minor: script assumes `getent` (glibc). On Alpine-based hosts it may not exist; add a `command -v getent` guard or fallback to `dig +short`.
Nice-to-have: after `docker compose up -d`, could `sleep 5 && curl -sI https://${BASE}` to tell the user whether a cert was issued.
seed_data_creation: None. A disposable work dir under /tmp/change_domain_test/work with a synthetic .env and a fake `docker` binary was used.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Script /app/deploy/change-domain.sh behaves correctly for both the happy path (DuckDNS-like domain whose A record matches SERVER_IP) and the guard path (DNS mismatch -> exit 1, no mutation). Live server at IP_SERVER confirmed to serve HTTP redirect on :80 but fail TLS handshake on :443 (no cert), confirming the Let's Encrypt / sslip.io PSL issue. No code changes made.
rca of the issue: Browser error ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR on https://crm.IP-SERVER.sslip.io is caused by Caddy on the VPS being unable to obtain a Let's Encrypt certificate for a *.sslip.io hostname. sslip.io is not on the Public Suffix List, so all its subdomains share one global LE certificates-per-registered-domain weekly quota, which is routinely exhausted. Reproduction: curl -v https://crm.IP-SERVER.sslip.io/ returns 'TLSv1.3 alert internal error' with no ServerHello cert. Mitigation: use /app/deploy/change-domain.sh <duckdns-or-own-domain> to point APP/N8N/WAHA domains at a PSL-listed base domain whose A records point to SERVER_IP; the script validates DNS, backs up .env, rewrites domain vars + N8N_*_WEBHOOK_URL hosts, and runs `docker compose up -d --build web backend n8n` so the frontend is rebuilt with the new REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL and Caddy requests a fresh cert.
